Time to get underway! Chamari Atapattu and Hasini Perera are the openers for Sri Lanka. Megan Schutt to kick off proceedings. A slip is in place. The countdown ends and the match begins. Here we go...
Both sets of players are coming out in the centre and will first stand in respect of their respective national anthems.

Pitch report - It's hard in nature and you can feel it's quite firm. The batters and bowlers get excited about the extra bounce at W.A.C.A. but the bowlers need to worry about their lines and lengths. There are footmarks on the surface and the ball might skid on and there can be variable bounce as well.

Australia (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (WK), Beth Mooney, Ashleigh Gardner, Meg Lanning (C), Ellyse Perry, Rachael Haynes, Nicola Carey (In for Annabel Sutherland), Jess Jonassen, Delissa Kimmince, Molly Strano, Megan Schutt.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Chamari Atapattu (C), Hasini Perera, Harshitha Madavi, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Shashikala Siriwardene, Nilakshi de Silva, Ama Kanchana, Kavisha Dilhari, Sugandika Kumari, Udeshika Prabodhani, Umesha Thimashini (In for Achini Kulasuriya).

Australian skipper, Meg Lanning, says that she would have bowled anyway as it's a new deck today and will stay true throughout the whole game. On her 100th T20I match, Meg smiles and replies that it's about the longevity about playing the game and considers it a vital match. Terms it a typical W.A.C.A. pitch with a decent amount of grass. Informs that they also have made a single change - Nicola Carey is in for Annabel Sutherland.

Sri Lankan skipper, Chamari Atapattu, says that she has chosen to bat as she is confident about her batting unit. Wants to play positive cricket. Adds that beating Australia is their target as they have not done that before. Informs about the one change - Umesha Thimashini comes in for Achini Kulasuriya. On her personal good form against Australia, Chamari Atapattu replies there is no secret as she tries to play her normal game with courage.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it comes down in favour of Chamari Atapattu. SRI LANKA WILL BAT!

Hello and welcome everyone for Match 5 of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2020 between Australia and Sri Lanka in Perth. Both teams faced defeats in their opening encounters and would be looking for their first win of this campaign. The reigning champions will be hurt after going down against India and they have a point to prove. For Sri Lanka, they are not the favourites, so they don't have the pressure of that tag and can express themselves with more freedom. On paper, the Islanders are light on experience and they would have to play out of their skins to compete with the home team. Stay tuned for more...
